title: Fix Record Schema
description: Schema for fixes/<id>/fix.yaml — the single artifact of the defect lane. A fix that restores already-established behavior carries this one record instead of the five-artifact feature contract. Area-agnostic: the shape is the same for api, cli, ui, and data projects, so this lives in governance/schemas/ rather than governance/<area>/schemas/.

id.description: Slug identifying this fix; must match the fixes/<id>/ directory name.

summary.description: One line stating the defect, in the language of the affected behavior.

expectation.description: Eligibility condition 1 — what already established the behavior being restored. A fix that cannot cite a source is introducing behavior, not restoring it, and belongs in the feature lane.

source.description: Repo-relative path to the requirement, contract, ADR, or spec that established the behavior. Must resolve — govkit validate checks it.

reference.description: The specific scenario, section, or clause within that source.

failure.description: What was actually observed, and where it was reported.

surface.description: What the fix touches. Cross-checked against the risk flags below.

paths.description: Repo-relative paths changed by this fix.

reproduction.description: Eligibility condition 2 — the test that fails before the fix and passes after.

test.description: Repo-relative path to the reproduction or regression test. Must resolve — govkit validate checks it.

scenario.description: The specific test case name within that file.

risk.description: Eligibility condition 4. Every flag is required so an omission cannot be read as false. Each is cross-checked against surface.paths in both directions: a false beside a change in that area fails, and so does a true — a true means the change belongs in the feature lane, not this one.

introduces_new_behavior.description: Eligibility condition 3. Must be false to stay in this lane; true promotes the change to the feature lane.

evidence.description: Optional references supporting the fix — CI run, before/after capture, profiling output.
